title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless core is coming to Claude — the 5th spec release drops sessions for request/response
bullets.summary: Anthropic is bringing the newest MCP spec to Claude: a stateless request/response core (handshake + session-ID removed) that lets servers run on serverless/edge, with hardened authorization and graduated official extensions; MCP has now crossed 400M monthly SDK downloads (4x this year).
bullets.how: Our Construct MCP fleet (Hermes, B9, PRAGMA connectors) can move to cheap stateless serverless deploys with cleaner auth; re-check each internal server against the 2026-07-28 auth hardening before publishing any to the directory.

bullets.title: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash to GA; OpenAI opens GPT-5.6 'Sol Ultrafast' invite-only preview
bullets.summary: Gemini 3.7 Flash is generally available (1M-token input, tool-calling + computer-control, tuned for coding and autonomous business workflows), while OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast tier (~750 output tokens/sec) is still invite-only — so only Google's is shippable today.
bullets.how: Route high-volume B9 batch text/image and computer-use jobs to Gemini 3.7 Flash now (GA + cheap + tool-calling); keep Sol Ultrafast benched until access clears, and keep model routing abstract under the sub-agents so we swap the best-of-week engine.

bullets.title: Perplexity closes a $300M Series E — enterprise research outgrowing consumer
bullets.summary: Perplexity raised $300M Series E, with enterprise subscriptions (Deep Research for competitive intel, technical research, regulatory monitoring) outgrowing the consumer product and the raise funding the enterprise roadmap plus direct API access.
bullets.how: Validates PRAGMA's 'AI research/monitoring as a paid enterprise workflow' thesis and gives Scout/Lens a benchmark; watch Perplexity's Deep Research API as a possible sourced-answer engine for our visibility scans.

bullets.title: arXiv — PlanBench-XL: long-horizon planning of tool-use agents in large-scale tool ecosystems
bullets.summary: A benchmark for how well LLM agents plan and select the right tools when the ecosystem is large (hundreds of MCP tools), exposing where agents mis-route or lose the thread over long horizons.
bullets.how: Directly on-point as our MCP tool count balloons: it argues for tool-scoping / retrieval over 'expose everything,' the discipline our sub-agents need to avoid mis-routing across the growing Construct fleet.

praxis_lesson: The plumbing is standardizing under us — MCP's stateless 2026-07-28 core is landing in Claude and clearing 400M downloads, and the frontier (Gemini 3.7 Flash GA, Sol Ultrafast) is a swappable, commoditizing layer. The durable edge stays one level up: keep model routing abstract, move our own servers to the new stateless/auth-hardened spec, and — per PlanBench-XL — scope which tools each agent sees rather than exposing the whole fleet, so orchestration stays reliable as the tool count grows.
